summary: This article explains how the octopus uses its soft, boneless body, sucker-covered arms, color-changing skin, ink and unusual brain to survive in the sea, and why scientists call it clever.
introduce: Read the title “The Clever Octopus” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: an animal with a soft body and no backbone, like a snail or a clam
colors or shapes that help an animal blend in with what is around it
the way the surface of something feels, such as smooth or bumpy

challengeTerms.def: an animal that has no backbone
a natural substance that gives something its color
a nerve cell that carries messages through the body

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that an octopus is smarter than most people think? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how an octopus uses camouflage and ink together to stay safe from predators.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review mollusk, camouflage, and texture, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use invertebrate, pigment, and neuron in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
